newsitem.title: USA: U.S. prisoner executed despite pope's plea.
newsitem.headline: U.S. prisoner executed despite pope's plea.

text.p: Hours after he was married, convicted rapist and murderer Joseph Roger O'Dell was executed by lethal injection on Wednesday despite pleas for mercy from Pope John Paul II.
The execution took place after Virginia Gov. George Allen turned down his clemency petition and the U.S. Supreme Court by a 9-0 vote rejected his last-minute appeal.
"Gov. Allen you're killing an innocent man," O'Dell said in a final statement.
O'Dell, who was administered a lethal injection at about 9:10 p.m. EDT (0110 GMT) and declared dead six minutes later, also said his final day was the happiest of his life.
He was married to longtime friend Lori Urs in a wedding ceremony at the Greensville Correctional Centre eight hours before he was put to death.

The execution was carried out despite widespread international protest, particularly in Italy where O'Dell became a focal point for Italian opposition to capital punishment. Many Italian journalists were outside the prison where the execution took place.

O'Dell was executed for the murder of Helen Schartner of Virginia Beach, whose body was found on Feb. 5, 1985, in a field near a nightclub where she had gone dancing the night before. She had been pistol-whipped, raped, sodomized and strangled.
"I want to say this to Eddie Schartner, the victim's son:" O'Dell said in his final statement. "Eddie, I did not kill your mother."

O'Dell appeared haggard and frightened as he was strapped to a gurney. At one point, Sister Helen Prejean, author of "Dead Man Walking" and his spiritual adviser, leaned over and placed her hands on his chest as if blessing him.

A career criminal, O'Dell was on parole from Florida on robbery and kidnapping charges when he abducted and killed Schartner in Virginia. Schartner, 44, was an employee of Virginia Natural Gas and the divorced mother of one.
He was arrested after leaving some bloody clothing, including a shirt and jacket, at a girlfriend's house. She turned him in after learning the slaying had occurred near clubs O'Dell frequented.
In their Supreme Court appeal, O'Dell's lawyers argued that state-of-the-art testing of sperm and semen samples recovered from the victim's body could prove his innocence.
But state lawyers replied that O'Dell's conviction and death sentence were upheld in countless legal proceedings.
O'Dell, 55, was married to Urs, 41, his volunteer paralegal, in a midday wedding. He remained behind bars and the couple was not allowed to touch, a prison spokesman said.

The ceremony was conducted by the Rev. Russell Ford, a former prison chaplain who has known O'Dell for many years. It was O'Dell's fourth marriage and Urs' second. As his wife, Urs will be entitled to claim his body.
Italian interest in the O'Dell case had bewildered and annoyed Schartner's family. "It's just like the Italians hate us," her sister, Gail Lee, told the Norfolk Virginian Pilot newspaper.

"I used to have great respect for that country and its history and its art ... now I never want to go there. I never want to set foot on their soil. Because by listening to just one side of this case, they in essence have said to my family, 'You are worthless. Helen's life didn't matter.'"

The pope and Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi appealed to halt the execution of O'Dell, who had no known ties to Italy but was made an honorary citizen of the city of Palermo and said he wanted to be buried there.
Before the execution hundreds of Italians opposed to capital punishment held a countdown vigil in Rome's Campo de Fiori square after an earlier protest at the U.S. embassy.
"Maybe the pope will call the governor (of Virginia)," one woman in the crowd said minutes before O'Dell was executed. "That's the only thing that might save him at this point."
But she and others in the small crowed broke into tears when, via a live television hook-up from Virginia, they heard a spokesman for Allen announce dryly:
"The execution was completed at 9:16" p.m.
Italy, which has no death penalty in civilian criminal cases, is among the most vocal supporters of a worldwide ban on capital punishment.
